Flatten nested patchwork objects

Source: R/fmt_plot_utils.R
fmt_flatten.Rd

Recursively extract ordinary grid cells from nested patchwork objects and arrange them in a new patchwork, optionally selecting or reordering cells. flatten_patchwork() is the same function under its original name, kept for existing code.

Usage

fmt_flatten(plots, ..., select_inds = NULL, nrow_inds_order = NULL)

flatten_patchwork(plots, ..., select_inds = NULL, nrow_inds_order = NULL)

Arguments

plots

A ggplot, patchwork object, grob, or nested list of these objects.

...

Named layout arguments passed to patchwork::wrap_plots(), such as nrow, ncol, design, guides and axis_titles. Unknown, unnamed and duplicate arguments are rejected. Supply additional graphics in plots as a list.

select_inds

Integer indices applied after flattening. Positive indices select and may repeat plots; negative indices exclude plots. Zero is ignored. Missing, fractional, mixed-sign and out-of-range indices are rejected. Duplicate cell names matched by a character design are rejected; use an unnamed list to repeat cells by position in that design.

nrow_inds_order

Single positive integer, at most the number of selected plots, to reorder them by interleaving rows. Applied after selection; it does not set the output layout's nrow. With ceiling(n / nrow_inds_order) output columns for n selected cells, plots take the positions that byrow = FALSE with nrow = nrow_inds_order would give them; unlike byrow, the cells themselves are reordered, so tags then run across rows instead of down columns.

Value

A patchwork object with ordinary grid cells at one level. Insets and their main plot stay together and count as one cell for selection/reordering. Containers marked with patchwork::free() also remain intact.

Details

Top-level plot annotations and the guides, axes, axis_titles and tag_level settings are retained for patchwork input. Explicit arguments in ... override inherited settings; an explicit axes without axis_titles also drops the inherited axis_titles, which then follows axes as in wrap_plots(). Grid geometry (dimensions, widths, heights and design) is rebuilt using ...; nested annotation and tagging scopes are not promoted. Selection indices refer to the extracted cells, including spacers, guide areas and wrapped graphics. A main plot with its insets, or a protected free() container, occupies one selection index. Named list entries that produce one cell retain their name; names inside nested lists are retained without container-name prefixes. These cell names can be matched to a character layout design by wrap_plots().

Tags from plot_annotation(tag_levels), including custom tag vectors, are assigned in output order, so they follow select_inds and nrow_inds_order rather than the original positions.

Insets are emitted alongside ordinary hosts at the same layout level, allowing shared axes and axis titles to be collected. Composite inset hosts remain intact. The returned object's length() and [[ follow native patchwork child indexing and include inset objects; selection and row interleaving use complete cells, including each host's insets. Nested lists are unwrapped before binding each inset to its preceding host, so list and patchwork inputs retain the same inset boundaries.

Flattening ordinary containers removes their nested collection scopes, including inner guides = "keep" or guides = "collect" settings. Collection is determined by the retained top-level settings and .... Guide areas move to the same output level; when collecting guides, patchwork uses only the first guide area if several are present. Use patchwork::wrap_elements(full = group) to retain an entire group, including its nested collection scopes, as one wrapped cell.

See also

Other plot formatting: fmt_axis(), fmt_axisText(), fmt_axisTile(), fmt_bg(), fmt_boxplot(), fmt_com(), fmt_expand(), fmt_his(), fmt_legend(), fmt_panel(), fmt_plot(), fmt_plot_base(), fmt_point(), fmt_raster(), fmt_ref(), fmt_scale(), fmt_strip(), fmt_strip2(), fmt_tag(), fmt_text()

Examples

library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
p1 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, disp)) + geom_point()
p2 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(gear, disp, group = gear)) + geom_boxplot()
p3 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(factor(gear))) + geom_bar()
p4 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(factor(cyl), mpg)) + geom_violin()

# \donttest{
# Flatten nested patchwork
nested <- (p1 | p2) / (p3 | p4)
fmt_flatten(nested, nrow = 1)


# Select specific sub-plots
fmt_flatten(nested, select_inds = c(1, 3))


# Interleave indices 1, 3, 2, 4, then arrange in two columns
fmt_flatten(nested, nrow_inds_order = 2, ncol = 2)


# Retain the overall title and collect matching axis titles
annotated <- nested + plot_annotation(title = "Example plots")
fmt_flatten(annotated, ncol = 2, axis_titles = "collect")


# Names determine placement in a character design
fmt_flatten(list(B = p2, A = p1), design = "AB")


# Keep a composite inset host together
inset_group <- wrap_plots(list(p1 | p2)) +
  inset_element(p3, .5, .5, 1, 1, align_to = "full")
fmt_flatten(list(inset_group, p4), ncol = 2)


# Retain a nested guide scope inside a wrapped cell
kept_group <- (p1 | p2) + plot_layout(guides = "keep")
fmt_flatten(list(wrap_elements(full = kept_group), p3), guides = "collect")

# }
